sourceBoundary: Original AAS2 supplementary questions. These are not mapped to Macmillan Science Level 2 core scope unless independently confirmed.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about flowering plants is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about flowering plants is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Flowers turn directly into roots
Flowers take in all the water from soil
Flowers help many plants make seeds
proposedOptions: Flowers turn directly into roots
Flowers take in all the water from soil
Flowers help many plants make seeds
items.originalCorrectOption: Flowers help many plants make seeds
items.proposedCorrectOption: Flowers help many plants make seeds

proposedOptionRationales.a: Flowers do not turn directly into roots.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Flowers do not take in all the water from soil.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Flowers help many flowering plants reproduce by forming seeds.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about butterfly life cycle is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about butterfly life cycle is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A butterfly begins life as an egg
A butterfly begins life as a seed
A butterfly begins life as a small bird
proposedOptions: A butterfly begins life as an egg
A butterfly begins life as a seed
A butterfly begins life as a small bird
items.originalCorrectOption: A butterfly begins life as an egg
items.proposedCorrectOption: A butterfly begins life as an egg

proposedOptionRationales.a: A butterfly develops from an egg.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Seeds grow into plants, not butterflies.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Butterflies are insects, not birds.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about photosynthesis is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about photosynthesis is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Plants get all their food from soil
Green plants take in oxygen to make food
Green plants take in carbon dioxide
proposedOptions: Plants get all their food from soil
Green plants take in oxygen to make food
Green plants take in carbon dioxide
items.originalCorrectOption: Green plants take in carbon dioxide
items.proposedCorrectOption: Green plants take in carbon dioxide

proposedOptionRationales.a: Soil provides minerals and support, but plants make sugars using light energy.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Green plants use carbon dioxide in photosynthesis and release oxygen; they do not use oxygen to make their food.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Green plants take in carbon dioxide from the air for photosynthesis.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about polar habitats is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about polar habitats is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Polar bears live in tropical rainforests
Polar bears live in Antarctica
Polar bears live in Arctic habitats
proposedOptions: Polar bears live in tropical rainforests
Polar bears live in Antarctica
Polar bears live in Arctic habitats
items.originalCorrectOption: Polar bears live in Arctic habitats
items.proposedCorrectOption: Polar bears live in Arctic habitats

proposedOptionRationales.a: Polar bears are adapted to Arctic habitats, not tropical rainforests.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Polar bears do not live naturally in Antarctica.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Polar bears live in Arctic regions.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about food chains is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about food chains is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A food chain shows how water freezes
A food chain shows how energy moves between organisms
A food chain shows how rocks are made
proposedOptions: A food chain shows how water freezes
A food chain shows how energy moves between organisms
A food chain shows how rocks are made
items.originalCorrectOption: A food chain shows how energy moves between organisms
items.proposedCorrectOption: A food chain shows how energy moves between organisms

proposedOptionRationales.a: A food chain is not about freezing water.
proposedOptionRationales.b: A food chain shows how food and energy pass between living things.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Rocks are not the focus of a food chain.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about herbivores is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about herbivores is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Rabbits are omnivores
Rabbits are carnivores
Rabbits are herbivores
proposedOptions: Rabbits are omnivores
Rabbits are carnivores
Rabbits are herbivores
items.originalCorrectOption: Rabbits are herbivores
items.proposedCorrectOption: Rabbits are herbivores

proposedOptionRationales.a: Rabbits mainly eat plants, so they are not omnivores.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Rabbits do not eat other animals as their main food source.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Rabbits are herbivores because they eat plants.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about circulation is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about circulation is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: The heart pumps blood around the body
The stomach pumps blood around the body
The lungs pump blood around the body
proposedOptions: The heart pumps blood around the body
The stomach pumps blood around the body
The lungs pump blood around the body
items.originalCorrectOption: The heart pumps blood around the body
items.proposedCorrectOption: The heart pumps blood around the body

proposedOptionRationales.a: The heart pumps blood around the body.
proposedOptionRationales.b: The stomach helps digest food.
proposedOptionRationales.c: The lungs help us breathe.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about nutrition is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about nutrition is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A balanced diet contains just one type of food
A balanced diet contains only sweets
A balanced diet provides different nutrients
proposedOptions: A balanced diet contains just one type of food
A balanced diet contains only sweets
A balanced diet provides different nutrients
items.originalCorrectOption: A balanced diet provides different nutrients
items.proposedCorrectOption: A balanced diet provides different nutrients

proposedOptionRationales.a: A balanced diet includes different foods and nutrients.
proposedOptionRationales.b: A diet of only sweets is not balanced.
proposedOptionRationales.c: A balanced diet provides a variety of nutrients.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about breathing is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about breathing is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: The lungs help us breathe
The stomach helps us breathe
The liver helps us breathe
proposedOptions: The lungs help us breathe
The stomach helps us breathe
The liver helps us breathe
items.originalCorrectOption: The lungs help us breathe
items.proposedCorrectOption: The lungs help us breathe

proposedOptionRationales.a: The lungs are the main organs used for breathing.
proposedOptionRationales.b: The stomach digests food.
proposedOptionRationales.c: The liver has other functions; it is not the main breathing organ.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about hygiene is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about hygiene is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Soap and water help remove germs
Soap adds germs to our hands
Perfume and dry air remove all germs
proposedOptions: Soap and water help remove germs
Soap adds germs to our hands
Perfume and dry air remove all germs
items.originalCorrectOption: Soap and water help remove germs
items.proposedCorrectOption: Soap and water help remove germs

proposedOptionRationales.a: Soap and water help remove dirt and many germs from hands.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Soap does not add germs when used properly.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Perfume does not remove germs and dry air is not a hand-cleaning method.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about solids is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about solids is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Solids take the shape of every container
Solids always flow like liquids
Solids keep their own shape
proposedOptions: Solids take the shape of every container
Solids always flow like liquids
Solids keep their own shape
items.originalCorrectOption: Solids keep their own shape
items.proposedCorrectOption: Solids keep their own shape

proposedOptionRationales.a: Solids generally keep their own shape.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Solids do not take the shape of every container.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Solids do not flow like liquids.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about freezing is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about freezing is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Freezing changes water into steam
Freezing changes liquid water into water vapour
Freezing changes liquid water into ice
proposedOptions: Freezing changes water into steam
Freezing changes liquid water into water vapour
Freezing changes liquid water into ice
items.originalCorrectOption: Freezing changes liquid water into ice
items.proposedCorrectOption: Freezing changes liquid water into ice

proposedOptionRationales.a: Freezing does not change water into steam.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Water vapour forms by evaporation, not freezing.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Freezing changes liquid water into solid ice.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about heat conductors is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about heat conductors is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Plastic is always a better heat conductor than metal
Metal transfers heat well
Wood transfers heat better than metal
proposedOptions: Plastic is always a better heat conductor than metal
Metal transfers heat well
Wood transfers heat better than metal
items.originalCorrectOption: Metal transfers heat well
items.proposedCorrectOption: Metal transfers heat well

proposedOptionRationales.a: Plastic is generally a poor heat conductor compared with metal.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Metal transfers heat well and is a good conductor.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Wood is generally a poorer heat conductor than metal.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about gravity is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about gravity is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Gravity only works on very heavy objects
Gravity pushes objects away from Earth
Gravity pulls objects towards Earth
proposedOptions: Gravity only works on very heavy objects
Gravity pushes objects away from Earth
Gravity pulls objects towards Earth
items.originalCorrectOption: Gravity pulls objects towards Earth
items.proposedCorrectOption: Gravity pulls objects towards Earth

proposedOptionRationales.a: Gravity acts on objects of different masses, not only very heavy ones.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth rather than pushing them away.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Near Earth's surface, gravity pulls objects toward Earth.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about ramps is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about a ramp is correct?
originalOptions: A ramp removes the force of gravity
A ramp makes a toy car heavier
A steeper ramp can make a toy car move faster
proposedOptions: A ramp is a sloping surface that can help move an object up or down
A ramp removes the force of gravity
A ramp makes an object heavier
items.originalCorrectOption: A steeper ramp can make a toy car move faster
items.proposedCorrectOption: A ramp is a sloping surface that can help move an object up or down

proposedOptionRationales.a: A ramp is a sloping surface that can help move an object between heights.
proposedOptionRationales.b: A ramp does not remove gravity.
proposedOptionRationales.c: A ramp does not make an object heavier.

items.revisionNote: Replaces an overgeneralised claim that a steeper ramp always makes a toy car faster.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about Earth rotation is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about Earth rotation is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Earth's rotation causes day and night
The Moon's orbit causes day and night
Earth's revolution around the Sun causes day and night
proposedOptions: Earth's rotation causes day and night
The Moon's orbit causes day and night
Earth's revolution around the Sun causes day and night
items.originalCorrectOption: Earth's rotation causes day and night
items.proposedCorrectOption: Earth's rotation causes day and night

proposedOptionRationales.a: Earth's rotation on its axis causes the cycle of day and night.
proposedOptionRationales.b: The Moon's orbit around Earth does not cause day and night.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Earth's revolution around the Sun causes a year, not the daily cycle of day and night.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about light sources is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about light sources is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A mirror creates its own light
The Sun is a natural source of light
The Moon makes its own light
proposedOptions: A mirror creates its own light
The Sun is a natural source of light
The Moon makes its own light
items.originalCorrectOption: The Sun is a natural source of light
items.proposedCorrectOption: The Sun is a natural source of light

proposedOptionRationales.a: A mirror reflects light; it does not create its own light.
proposedOptionRationales.b: The Sun is a natural source of light.
proposedOptionRationales.c: The Moon reflects sunlight and does not make its own light.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about water cycle is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about water cycle is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour
Evaporation changes water vapour into rocks
Evaporation changes liquid water into ice
proposedOptions: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour
Evaporation changes water vapour into rocks
Evaporation changes liquid water into ice
items.originalCorrectOption: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour
items.proposedCorrectOption: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour

proposedOptionRationales.a: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Water vapour does not change into rocks by evaporation.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Freezing changes liquid water into ice.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about recycling is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about recycling is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Recycling paper helps reduce waste
Throwing paper away is the same as recycling
Burning paper is the best way to recycle it
proposedOptions: Recycling paper helps reduce waste
Throwing paper away is the same as recycling
Burning paper is the best way to recycle it
items.originalCorrectOption: Recycling paper helps reduce waste
items.proposedCorrectOption: Recycling paper helps reduce waste

proposedOptionRationales.a: Recycling paper can reduce waste and the need for new materials.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Throwing paper away is not recycling.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Burning paper creates smoke and is not the best recycling method.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about water conservation is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about water conservation is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: People and plants need clean water
Dirty water is always safe to drink
Only plants need clean water
proposedOptions: People and plants need clean water
Dirty water is always safe to drink
Only plants need clean water
items.originalCorrectOption: People and plants need clean water
items.proposedCorrectOption: People and plants need clean water

proposedOptionRationales.a: People and plants need clean water for health and growth.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Dirty water may contain harmful germs and is not always safe to drink.
proposedOptionRationales.c: People as well as plants need clean water.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about skeleton is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about skeleton is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs
The rib cage helps digest food
The rib cage protects the brain
proposedOptions: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs
The rib cage helps digest food
The rib cage protects the brain
items.originalCorrectOption: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs
items.proposedCorrectOption: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs

proposedOptionRationales.a: The rib cage helps protect the heart and lungs.
proposedOptionRationales.b: The rib cage does not digest food.
proposedOptionRationales.c: The skull protects the brain; the rib cage protects the chest organs.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about simple machines is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about simple machines is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A pulley is an inclined plane
A ramp is an example of an inclined plane
A lever is an inclined plane
proposedOptions: A pulley is an inclined plane
A ramp is an example of an inclined plane
A lever is an inclined plane
items.originalCorrectOption: A ramp is an example of an inclined plane
items.proposedCorrectOption: A ramp is an example of an inclined plane

proposedOptionRationales.a: A pulley and a lever are different simple machines.
proposedOptionRationales.b: A ramp is an example of an inclined plane.
proposedOptionRationales.c: A lever is not an inclined plane.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about shadows is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about shadows is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A shadow forms without any light
A shadow forms when an object blocks light
A shadow forms when sound is blocked
proposedOptions: A shadow forms without any light
A shadow forms when an object blocks light
A shadow forms when sound is blocked
items.originalCorrectOption: A shadow forms when an object blocks light
items.proposedCorrectOption: A shadow forms when an object blocks light

proposedOptionRationales.a: A shadow needs a light source; it does not form without light.
proposedOptionRationales.b: A shadow forms when an object blocks some light.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Sound is not light, so blocking sound does not make a shadow.

items.originalPrompt: Which statement about planets is scientifically correct?
items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about planets is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: Earth is the planet we live on
Earth is the Moon's natural satellite
Earth is a star
proposedOptions: Earth is the planet we live on
Earth is the Moon's natural satellite
Earth is a star
items.originalCorrectOption: Earth is the planet we live on
items.proposedCorrectOption: Earth is the planet we live on

proposedOptionRationales.a: Earth is the planet on which we live.
proposedOptionRationales.b: Earth is not the Moon's satellite; the Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
proposedOptionRationales.c: Earth is a planet, not a star.

items.proposedPrompt: Which statement about temperature is scientifically correct?
originalOptions: A thermometer measures temperature
A clock measures temperature
A ruler measures temperature
proposedOptions: A thermometer measures temperature
A clock measures temperature
A ruler measures temperature
items.originalCorrectOption: A thermometer measures temperature
items.proposedCorrectOption: A thermometer measures temperature

proposedOptionRationales.b: A clock measures time.
proposedOptionRationales.c: A ruler measures length.
